top20pct_sv_dims.interpretation: Top-20% SVD dims carry 57.3% of cosine mass but only 20.2% of discriminative signal — a 2.84× over-representation of object content in the score.

access_ratio.note: mass values are |cosine contribution| before summing, matching E2_direct_spectral.py's convention -- see compute_access_ratio() docstring for why this matters.
access_ratio.interpretation: Access ratio 0.484 (95% CI [0.448, 0.530]): the most discriminative 5% of dimensions receive 0.48× their proportional cosine weight (vs 1.0 for uniform, 1.07× for SV²-proportional null). Masking is reliable across bootstrap resamples (P=1.0000).

structural_argument: The 1.7% (ρ²) from the original Table 1 is a property of the MLP proxy, not of the geometric effect. The direct measurement shows: top-20% SVD dims carry 57.3% of cosine similarity mass but only 20.2% of per-dimension discriminability. This 2.84× amplification of object-level cosine mass over compositional-discriminative mass is the structural mechanism. The Spearman ρ² is the wrong statistic to report — it measures correlation between a scale-confounded proxy and rank, not the actual geometric suppression of compositional signal in the similarity score.
